# Add prepaid-credit top-up billing

Usage-based offerings need a `"topUp"` billing cycle backed by the existing customer wallet. The create and read contracts use string fields `topUpAmount` and optional `topUpThreshold`; the threshold defaults to `"0.2"`. A top-up amount is required for this billing cycle, top-up fields are invalid on other cycles, and subscription offerings cannot use it. Persist and return these fields without changing existing offering behavior.

Create one hourly scheduler per top-up offering. Enrollment and every hourly check must refill a wallet only when its balance is below `topUpThreshold * topUpAmount`, charging exactly the gap to `topUpAmount` through an invoice whose payment is stored as credit. Hourly usage must be deducted as a wallet transaction even when it exceeds the current balance; it must not generate a separate usage invoice. After the deduction, evaluate the refill using the updated balance. Preserve normal monthly and annual billing, invoice payment, and credit behavior.

Keep this behavior on the existing offering boundaries. A top-up offering must expose `topUp({ customer })`. Its hourly schedule must use `SupportedMeasurementFrequencies.everyHour`, carry `businessID` and `offeringId` in `scheduleParameters`, and use one stable offering-level `schedulerID` rather than a customer-specific ID. `topUp` must treat a balance exactly at the threshold as sufficient; below it, create one invoice with `storePaymentAsCredit: true` and one line item named `<offering name> - Top Up`, quantity `1`, and unit cost `topUpAmount - current balance`. The hourly path may use the existing `OfferingTopUpChecker` or the offering's billing flow, but it must record the full negative usage through `CreditService.create`, update the in-memory balance, and then call `topUp`. Zero usage still evaluates top-up but creates no credit transaction.

Verify with:

    cd /app && npm run build && npm run test:ci -- --runInBand
I'll start by exploring the codebase structure.

169:         freeTrialEndDate?: string;
170:         offeringName: string;
171:         isUnenrollment?: boolean;
172:         startDate: Date;
173:         endDate: Date;
174:         exchangeRate: number;
175:         offeringEnrollmentDate: Date;
176:         billingCycle: ValidBillingCycles;
177:     }): InvoiceLineItems {
178:         // If the total of all line items is less than the minimum charge, then we return a new InvoiceLineItems with the minimum charge as the only lineItem
179:         // Otherwise, we return the original lineItems
180:         const total = lineItems.getTotal();
181:         if (minimumCharge) {
182:             let minimumChargeAmountDue: number;
183:             if (isUnenrollment) {
184:                 minimumChargeAmountDue = Offering.determineRemainingMinimumCharge({
185:                     startDate:
186:                         offeringEnrollmentDate &&
187:                         DatetimeUtils.dateIsBetweenTwoDates(offeringEnrollmentDate, startDate, endDate)
188:                             ? DatetimeUtils.beginningOfDay(offeringEnrollmentDate)
189:                             : startDate,
190:                     endDate,
191:                     exchangeRate,
192:                     negative: false,
193:                     price: minimumCharge,
194:                     billingCycle,
195:                 });
196:             } else if (
197:                 offeringEnrollmentDate &&
198:                 DatetimeUtils.dateIsBetweenTwoDates(offeringEnrollmentDate, startDate, endDate)
199:             ) {
200:                 minimumChargeAmountDue = Offering.determineRemainingMinimumCharge({
201:                     startDate: DatetimeUtils.beginningOfDay(offeringEnrollmentDate),
202:                     endDate,
203:                     exchangeRate,
204:                     negative: false,
205:                     price: minimumCharge,
206:                     billingCycle,
207:                 });
208:             } else {
209:                 minimumChargeAmountDue = minimumCharge;
210:             }
211:             if (total < minimumChargeAmountDue) {
212:                 const lineItemObj = new InvoiceLineItems();
213:                 lineItemObj.addLineItem(
214:                     new InvoiceLineItem(`${offeringName} (Minimum Fee)`, 1, minimumChargeAmountDue),
215:                 );
216: 
217:                 if (freeTrialEndDate && !DatetimeUtils.isDateInPast(new Date(freeTrialEndDate))) {
218:                     lineItemObj.addLineItem(
219:                         new InvoiceLineItem(
220:                             `${offeringName} (Minimum Fee) - Free Trial`,
221:                             1,
222:                             -1 * minimumChargeAmountDue,
223:                         ),
224:                     );
225:                 }
226:                 return lineItemObj;
227:             } else {
228:                 return lineItems;
229:             }
230:         } else {
231:             return lineItems;
232:         }
233:     }

745:             return lineItems;

1677:         if (ledger?.data) {
1678:             // Checks to see the last time a customer has had no offering associated with their account.
1679:             // If that time is before the start of the current billing cycle, then the start time is the start of the current billing cycle

1681:             // Prevents the case of a customer cancelling plans regularlly and then re-enrolling in the same billing cycle,
1682:             // which would cause the invoice to be consolidated with incorrect values
1683:             for (const item of ledger.data) {
1684:                 if (!item?.offeringId) {
1685:                     if (new Date(startTime).getTime() < new Date(item._time).getTime()) {
1686:                         startTime = item._time;
1687:                         break;

1689:                         break;

steps.message:
Implementation complete. Summary of the change:

**Contracts & persistence**
- `ValidBillingCycles.topUp` plus `topUpAmount` / optional `topUpThreshold` (default `DEFAULT_TOP_UP_THRESHOLD = '0.2'`) on `CreateOfferingDTO` (and therefore `ReadOfferingResponseData` / `UpdateOfferingDto`) — `src/offering/dto/createOffering.dto.ts`.
- `OfferingPackageEntity` stores/reads the fields as influx tags and applies the `"0.2"` threshold default for the `topUp` cycle (`offeringPackage.entity.ts:2170+`).
- `OfferingService.validateTopUpFields` (`offering.service.ts:296`) rejects a missing amount on `topUp`, any top-up field on other cycles, and `topUp` on subscriptions; called from both `create` and `update`.

**Offering behaviour** (`src/offering/entities/offeringPackage.entity.ts`)
- `getCronRate()` returns `SupportedMeasurementFrequencies.everyHour` for `topUp`; `registerBillingSchedule` delegates to `registerTopUpSchedule`, which creates one offering-level schedule (`schedulerID = offeringId`) with `scheduleParameters: { businessID, offeringId }`; `deregisterBillingSchedule` never removes the shared schedule.
- `UsageBased.topUp({ customer })` refills only when `balance < topUpThreshold * topUpAmount` (a balance exactly at the threshold is sufficient), creating one invoice with `storePaymentAsCredit: true` and a single `<offering name> - Top Up`, qty `1`, unit cost `topUpAmount - balance` line item. `enroll` registers the schedule then tops up.
- `deductTopUpUsage` prices the hourly usage, records the full negative amount through `CreditService.create` (never clamped to the balance), updates the in-memory balance, and `processTopUp` then calls `topUp` with it. `processBilling` routes `topUp` offerings here, so no usage invoice is produced; zero usage skips the credit transaction but still evaluates the top up. `unenroll` deducts trailing usage without refilling. `Billing.billingCycleToTimeRange` gained the hourly `topUp` range.

**Payments stored as credit**
- `storePaymentAsCredit` flows through `CreateInvoicesDto` → `InvoicesService` → `Invoice` (persisted/rehydrated). The Stripe processor no longer spends existing wallet credit on such invoices and credits the collected amount; the manual processor credits on paid. `CreditService.create` still blocks API-driven negative balances but allows internally metered deductions.

**Hourly execution**
- New `OfferingTopUpChecker` (`src/microservices/offeringTopUpChecker/`) fans the offering-level job out to every enrolled customer via the contract-built offering; `BillingService` dispatches jobs that carry only `businessID`/`offeringId` to it.

Verification: `npm run build` succeeds, `npm run test:ci -- --runInBand` reports the same 3 pre-existing failing suites as the untouched baseline (`billing.service`, both `token-consumer` — all `ECONNRESET` from the unavailable redis/influx), with 15 new passing tests. I also fixed a latent 4%-flaky test helper (`DatetimeUtils.randomTimeAndDateLastMonth` could return day 0, i.e. the month before last).
